old: It may echo an ancient greeting wishing someone good health.
It once meant a simultaneous discharge of guns, first spelled with an 'a' instead of an 'o.'
Its root, salve, is the very word Romans used to say hello.
clues: This noun from the world of cannons and warships likely traces back to a Latin word for a salute, born from the everyday Roman greeting meaning 'hail.'
It names guns fired together in one coordinated burst, a single crash rather than a long continuous barrage, like a warship discharging its cannons at once.
Figuratively, a debater fires an 'opening' one: a first sharp burst of arguments or criticism aimed at an opponent.
